submission.reasoning: On workstation5, user WORKSTATION5\wardog opened an interactive cmd.exe (proc-29da349e7e) with high integrity. At 2020-10-23T06:36:43Z that shell started bitsadmin.exe (proc-826bdb1e01), which ran /transfer /Download /priority Foreground. The job pulled a remote file from raw.githubusercontent.com and saved it as C:\Users\wardog\AppData\Local\Temp\bitsadmin1_flag.ps1, a PowerShell script name in the user's Temp folder. This matches the Atomic Red Team T1197 test: BITS jobs abused for ingress tool transfer and defense evasion. The 'flag' filename suggests a security test, but I'm treating it as malicious because that is how the BITS technique works. A search for the file name found only the bitsadmin command line. The graph has no separate file entity and no record of anything running the script, and it has no network-connection entity to block.
